articles.title: Mariona Caldentey penalty provides late WCL relief for Arsenal against Køge
articles.summary: Mariona Caldentey’s 93rd-minute penalty delivered a win and a hefty dose of relief to fans bouncing behind the goal in the North Bank after the ball hit the back of the net, but Arsenal’s narrow defeat of HB Køge in their Champions League opener left more questions unanswered than answered for the…
body: Manager Renée Slegers’ puffed cheeks said it all when the full-time whistle went. If it had been revealed on the final whistle that a forcefield surrounded the opposition goal at Meadow Park, many would have believed it, such was the extent of Arsenal’s ridiculous profligacy in front of goal in their league phase opener.

Exactly what is stopping Arsenal from getting the ball in the back of the net with a swagger reflective of their talent-laden squad is hard to pinpoint. Yes, teams are defending excellently against them, as a battling Køge and goalkeeper Alberte Vingum did on Tuesday night, but this feels like an Arsenal problem: a mentality one, a training ground one, a ruthlessness one.
The shadow of Sunday’s trip to Stamford Bridge loomed large at Meadow Park with eight changes made to the team that salvaged a point against Manchester United deep into added time on Saturday.
Only centre-back pairing Leah Williamson and Steph Catley and forward Stina Blackstenius retained their place in the starting XI for their Champions League opener.

articles.title: Giants’ Jaxson Dart could reportedly miss rest of season with knee injury
articles.summary: Testing said to reveal injury is worse than anticipated. Quarterback was hurt against Rams on Monday. New York Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart will be out for an extended period of time and could miss the rest of the NFL season after suffering a knee injury in Monday night’s loss to the Los Angeles…
body: ESPN reported that the injury to Dart’s left knee was more severe than initially anticipated. Adam Schefter said further testing has left the Giants and Dart facing the possibility of season-ending surgery.

The second-year quarterback was hurt on the opening possession of the Giants’ 28-6 defeat to the Rams. Initial reports said that Dart sprained his MCL and avoided broken bones, with an MRI set for Tuesday. Head coach John Harbaugh said Monday that he believed a “devastating outcome” had been avoided and that he did not expect Dart to be out long-term without giving a further recovery timeline.

The 23-year-old started the season strong in New York’s Week 1 win over Dallas but left the field after taking a huge hit from Byron Young and Josaiah Stewart on the Giants’ seventh play Monday night. Dart watched the second half in a track suit on the sidelines. Jameis Winston could not get much going after Dart’s exit, throwing an end-zone interception as New York got all of their points from field goals.

articles.title: Will anyone topple Infantino? How Fifa president is trying to cling on after World Cup sell-off debacle
articles.summary: Fifa president continues to lobby for re-election despite no other candidates coming forward to challenge him. For Gianni Infantino there is no international break. The Fifa president is widely expected to make an appearance at the United Nations general assembly this week in New York, where he…
body: Infantino has not been idle during the lull since Fifa abandoned its World Cup sell-off plan last month, instead crisscrossing the globe on a private jet provided by Qatar Airways as part of its sponsorship deal with world football’s governing body.

From his strongholds in Doha, Rabat and Miami, Infantino has also visited Colombia, the Dominican Republic, Kyrgyzstan and various other countries, his trips often coinciding with the approval of funding for development projects worth millions of dollars. His would-be opponents have been conspicuous by their silence.

Whether Qatar Airways facilitating Infantino’s re-election campaign should be considered legitimate Fifa presidential business is a moot point, which neatly encapsulates the huge incumbency bias that will benefit Infantino if a vote takes place at the Fifa congress in March. That ballot appears to be in doubt, with multiple sources involved in the push to remove Infantino telling the Guardian they are running out of hope of finding a candidate to beat him.

articles.title: Wamser rescues point for Manchester City in WCL fightback at Bayern Munich
articles.summary: Manchester City produced a gutsy performance to fight back and earn a valuable 2-2 draw away at Bayern Munich on their return to the Champions League. José Barcala’s side took the lead through Giulia Gwinn and an unfortunate Kerstin Casparij own goal but Beth Mead and Carlotta Wamser earned the…
body: City’s head coach, Andrée Jeglertz, was pleased with the resolve of his side after a difficult first half. “It [a comeback] has happened before because we know the quality is there,” he said. “The mentality of ­winning and the belief is there. It shows ­something about this group again.

“There were definitely two phases of this game. In the first half, Bayern were very good. I think we were a bit slow on the ball … It was almost like we were surprised by the tempo. I know we weren’t but it looked like that. At the end of the first half, we got a little bit back. The trust and the belief at half-time was good so I felt that this is still possible.”

It was always going to be a challenging start for the English champions against a Bayern team who have historically thrived in the league phase of this competition. They came into this unbeaten in their last 15 home group-stage matches and on the back of a semi-final run last ­season that, according to Gwinn, had left them “even hungrier and eager for more”. Not only that but the German team have kicked off the defence of their Frauen-Bundesliga title in stunning fashion with five wins from five.

articles.title: GB boxers guaranteed three medals at Europeans
articles.summary: Britain guarantee at least three medals at the European Boxing Championships in Bulgaria as Chantelle Reid, Damar Thomas and Abdul Burton all reach the semi-finals.
body: Great Britain are guaranteed at least three medals at the European Boxing Championships in Bulgaria after Chantelle Reid, Damar Thomas and Abdul Burton reached the semi-finals.
Reid cruised to a 5-0 win over Ireland's Evelyn Igharo in a women's light-middleweight contest at the Asics Arena Sports Hall in Sofia.
The 28-year-old Commonwealth Games silver medallist will face Serbia's Milena Matovic in the last four on Wednesday.
Thomas won by the same margin in a men's super-heavyweight fight against Georgia's Nikoloz Begadze and the 21-year-old will take on Mahammad Abdullayev of Azerbaijan in the semi-finals.

articles.title: UTSA vs. Colorado State: Asaad Chapman leads 5 key players to watch
articles.summary: The Roadrunners' defense delivered against the Longhorns, as UTSA's cornerbacks showed why they are regarded as perhaps the team's strongest unit.
body: When UTSA coach Jeff Traylor reviewed the video from Saturday's loss to Texas, the Roadrunners' cornerbacks group jumped off the screen.

Matching up against a pair of potential future first-round NFL draft selections in Cam Coleman and Ryan Wingo, UTSA's defensive backs "competed their tails off" with pristine technique, Traylor said. The group created a few hiccups for the nation's No. 1-ranked team, even as Texas eventually pulled away for a 30-6 win in Austin.

While the entire Roadrunners defense gained confidence from Saturday's performance, Traylor said he's been especially pleased with UTSA's cornerbacks, noting that "the playbook is wide open when you've got corners that can cover."
"I would say it's exceeded even our expectations, and our expectations were pretty high," Traylor said. "Really happy for that room right now."

articles.title: What Does Jerry Jones Think of the Brazil Field Ahead of Cowboys-Ravens?
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys are heading into a very different kind of Week 3 test. After rolling past the Washington Commanders 37-20, the Cowboys now have to take its game overseas for a matchup with the Baltimore Ravens in Rio de Janeiro.
body: That concern has lingered because Maracanã Stadium recently hosted soccer events, with players raising questions about the condition of the natural grass. With the Cowboys and Ravens scheduled to play there Sunday, attention has turned toward whether the field will be ready for an NFL game.

The Cowboys owner and general manager, Jerry Jones, addressed the issue on Tuesday, September 22, during an appearance on 105.3 The Fan with The Athletic’s Jon Machota. Jones made it clear that he isn’t expecting the field to become a problem for the Cowboys or Ravens.
Jones said he is “comfortable” with the condition of the surface and believes the NFL will have it ready for the matchup.

“I have an interest in a lot of automobile dealerships in Sao Paulo as well as Rio. I have an associate that I’ve been partners with for 30 years. We’re the largest dealers in Brazil. So, I got a lot of good friends I’ll be saying hello to down there.”

body: The Leopards and the Warriors have had an ongoing dispute for almost 12 months, dating back to the high-profile ticketing saga that led to Leigh's owner Derek Beaumont saying his club would not participate in the fixture over a disagreement about their ticket allocation of 4,800.
They ultimately did play the game and were eliminated from the play-offs with Wigan winning 18-6.

With the Warriors set to host Wakefield in the play-off semi-final on Saturday, matters reignited again over the weekend after an original post from Wigan detailed ticketing arrangements for whichever side visited the Brick this weekend in the play-offs would receive an allocation of 5,000 tickets for safety reasons.
Leigh were beaten by Wakefield Trinity in their eliminator match, where a win for the Leopards would have seen them progress to face Wigan instead.

articles.title: Iowa football RBs discuss monster day vs. UNI
articles.summary: After a monstrous performance in Iowa 's 55-0 rout of Northern Iowa (2-1) on Saturday at Kinnick Stadium, running backs Xavier Williams and Nathan McNeil spoke afterwards about what led to the overall success of the ground game against the Panthers.
body: As a team, Iowa (3-0) rushed for a staggering 422 yards and six touchdowns. Williams led the backfield with 151 rushing yards and three touchdowns, followed by McNeil with 111 yards and two scores, and Braeden Jackson added 125 yards and a rushing touchdown. Jackson had a 24-yard touchdown reception, too. Those were the first touchdowns of McNeil and Jackson's Hawkeye careers.

"They make our job really easy. I think our O-line is second to none. We wanted to control more work last year, and I haven't seen much of a fall-off at all. So they make our jobs really easy," Williams said.

"I think our running back room is second to none in the country, and we kind of have that mentality going into every game, and it's really all about your opportunity. We knew we were going to get an opportunity today, and we were all very excited, and we stepped up, so it was good."

articles.title: Menzies reveals heart attack scare before Matchplay incident
articles.summary: Players Championship 29 winner Cameron Menzies has revealed he feared he was suffering a heart attack on a flight to Switzerland, prompting him to take a serious look at his lifestyle.
body: Menzies saw off Gian van Veen 8-4 in the final to claim his second ProTour title of 2026 on Tuesday.
Menzies continued his sparkling Players Championship form to claim a fourth PDC ranking title at Maassport Den Bosch, after an impressive string of seven straight wins.

After capturing his second title of the year, the Scot, reflected on his medical episode in Blackpool when he was forced to withdraw from the tournament after being taken ill during his second-round match against Ross Smith.

"Even before [the incident] happened, as you can see I've lost a bit of weight. Last year I was heading to Switzerland and I genuinely thought I was having a heart attack on the plane," explained Menzies. "I went for scans because heart problems is something that runs in my family.

articles.title: 'Outstanding' Jacks 'growing in new role' after five-for vs Sri Lanka
articles.summary: Will Jacks was hailed as "outstanding" by England white-ball captain Harry Brook on Tuesday night as he took five wickets to spur his side to an 89-run victory against Sri Lanka.
body: Jacks starred with both bat and ball as England took a 1-0 lead in the three-match ODI series, with the batting all-rounder moving England to 265 all out in the first innings, with an unbeaten 46 off 47.
In the 48th over, the 27-year-old, who has been moved down the order, ruthlessly smashed Dushmantha Chameera for four consecutive fours, making a score of 18 off the over.
He was brought on to bowl in the 20th over of Sri Lanka's innings, and would end the day with career-best figures of 5-22 from seven overs.
"He's really growing into this role," Brook said of Jacks. "He's bought into everything that we want to do, as have the other boys.
